question.problem:
Find ${lim}_{t\to 0}[f(t)+g(t)]$ given that $f(t)$ and $g(t)$ are defined as:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t)=[\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} \\ {e}^{t} \\ \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{t}\end{aligned}],\,g(t)=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ 1 \\ \frac{2t-1}{{t}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the limit of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 0}f(t)=[\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 0}{t}^{2} \\ {lim}_{t\to 0}{e}^{t} \\ {lim}_{t\to 0}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{t}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{0}^{2} \\ {e}^{0} \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Note that the third component is a special limit.

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 0}g(t)=[\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 0}\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ {lim}_{t\to 0}1 \\ {lim}_{t\to 0}\frac{2t-1}{{t}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡0 \\ 1 \\ \frac{2(0)-1}{{0}^{2}+1})\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use properties of limits to calculate the final result:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 0}[f(t)+g(t)] & ={lim}_{t\to 0}f(t)+{lim}_{t\to 0}g(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
